answer: The currier counts the slicker strokes on every hide he dresses and enters the count in his tally against the hide. A dune hide dressed elsewhere fails the tally: at the falcon of the slicker the strokes must match the currier's own hand, and a strange hide cracks in the cold. Forging a dressing means hiring a currier, buying false oil and paying 5,600, and the quartz entry in the stroke tally is checked at every saddler's, so a hide whose strokes were never counted is refused.
